dedupe_keys.name: extreme event resilience of rail truck intermodal freight networks framework and case application rice university

description: This study by Sushreyo Misra and Jamie Padgett of Rice University, published in the Journal of Infrastructure Systems in 2022, introduces a framework for the time-evolving functionality and resilience of rail-truck intermodal freight networks hit by regional disruptions such as natural hazards, and applies it in a case study. The framework draws on publicly available datasets and probabilistic models to estimate the damage and functionality of network components. It proposes new restoration models that link physical damage to functionality, improving on earlier work, and it counts the functionality of intermodal terminals alongside the highway and railway networks. The framework gives network throughput and functionality metrics at points along the recovery timeline and can be extended to the wider economic impacts of freight disruption on communities. Access: journal article. Licence and cost: subscription. Caveats: only the abstract was read, so the study region, hazard scenario and data sources are not described here. It informs resilience, hazard exposure and network flow analysis of multimodal freight systems. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework and the inland waterway routing case study in the catalogue.
